comment.comment:
been looking more closely at the hooked vs bordr comparison. bordr is building legitimate tech and the axiom integration is a big win. i still think hooked is by far the better bet at current valuations.

start with adoption and valuation. hooked has over 1,000 launches using 50 different rules. bordr has around 100. hooked has already demonstrated meaningful trading activity, generated millions in buybacks and burns, and established a much larger ecosystem. yet bordr trades at $5m while hooked sits around $3.3m. you're paying 50% more for the platform with a fraction of the demonstrated adoption.

then consider value capture. on a typical hooked meteora curve, every $1m of volume generates $6,800 in $hooked market buys and permanent burns. on bordr's standard plain launch, the same volume generates around $2,750 in buybacks, with the tokens held in treasury. hooked has already burned over 64m tokens, more than 6% of the original supply.

and hooked has two paths to dominate this market. token-2022 hooks already work with existing solana infrastructure. hooked also has its own programmable token standard and dex, supporting more sophisticated mechanics that token-2022 can't handle like bordrless is building, but there's a reason hooked has found so much more adoption today, because it's building products that are useful today. ultimately the winner here will be the platform with the largest network effects and currently there is no comparison, it's hooked.

the biggest advantage is the dev and the product philosophy. every day hooked ships new mechanics with the potential to spawn an entirely new meta. ai-generated hooks, autonomous agents, on-chain games, lending, options, programmable trading restrictions, and increasingly sophisticated combinations of all of them. every new mechanic gives creators another reason to launch on hooked and traders another reason to pay attention.

the ultimate winner of the launchpad wars will be the platform that can adapt to whatever comes next. hooked is already building that.

at $3m market cap with actual adoption, demonstrated buybacks, an expanding product, and a cracked dev shipping nonstop, i think the opportunity here is enormous.

most of this downtrend has been driven by a broader crypto sell off, this final capitulation leg driven by the the bordr vamp attempt is probably needed to shake out the last of the weak hands. if you're stressing out about it i recommend you log off and let your bag marinate.
